s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute neurological deterioration with fever and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: Altered mental status
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness
Hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule on brain MRI
Pleocytosis and elevated protein in cerebrospinal fluid
Progression of neurological deficits and imaging findings despite empirical antibiotic treatment
key_facts: 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Transferred for evaluation of altered mental status
Minimally responsive and febrile on arrival
Glasgow Coma Scale 10
Required intubation for airway protection
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
No meningeal signs
Vital signs were stable
Leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT showed hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect
Brain MRI showed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule
Lumbar puncture yielded cerebrospinal fluid with 538 WBCs/mm³ and protein 81 mg/dL
Empirical IV ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir were begun
Leukocytosis improved but fever persisted
Repeat lumbar puncture showed increased opening pressure and pleocytosis
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Focal neurological deficits and hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT

shortlist.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use increase risk of opportunistic infections

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state due to hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use

shortlist.label: Cerebral Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Focal neurological deficits and mass effect on head CT, with potential for lymphoma in immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Cerebral Nocardiosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, focal neurological deficits, and hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT, with potential for Nocardia infection in immunocompromised patient

raw.rationale: The patient's history of intravenous heroin use and hepatitis C suggests a compromised immune system, making him susceptible to opportunistic infections like toxoplasmosis. The presence of hypodense areas in the basal ganglia on CT and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity on MRI, along with the clinical presentation of altered mental status and focal neurological deficits, are consistent with cerebral toxoplasmosis. The lack of response to empirical antibiotics and the progression of symptoms despite treatment also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Brain Abscess
rejected.why: The absence of ring enhancement on MRI and the lack of significant improvement with empirical antibiotics make brain abscess less likely

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: While the patient's immune status is compromised, the clinical and radiological findings do not typically match those of PML, which usually presents with asymmetric white matter lesions

rejected.label: Cerebral Lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and imaging findings are not typical for cerebral lymphoma, which often presents with more homogeneous enhancement and a different demographic profile

rejected.label: Cerebral Nocardiosis
rejected.why: The lack of specific risk factors for nocardiosis, such as lung disease or a history of steroid use, and the absence of characteristic imaging features like abscesses or nodules, make this diagnosis less likely
